name: Alkanes
physicalProperties: Non-polar; mp/bp increase with chain length; branching ↓ bp; insoluble in water, soluble in non-polar solvents; density <1 g/mL; IR: ~2850-2960 cm⁻¹ (sp³ C-H)
chemicalProperties: Low reactivity; combustion → CO2+H2O; free-radical halogenation (Cl2/hv, Br2/hv); cracking (high T, catalyst); isomerization

name: Alkenes
hybridization: sp² at C=C (120° trigonal planar); sp³ elsewhere
geometry: Planar around double bond; cis/trans (E/Z) isomerism possible
bondType: One σ + one π (C=C); π is weaker, reactive site
physicalProperties: Similar to alkanes but slightly more polarizable; bp slightly ↑ vs alkane; IR: 3080 cm⁻¹ (=C-H), 1650 cm⁻¹ (C=C), 890-990 cm⁻¹ (=C-H bend); ¹H NMR vinyl H δ 4.5-6.5 ppm
reactions: C2H4 + Br2 → CH2Br-CH2Br (halogenation, anti-addition, decolorizes Br2)
C3H6 + HBr → CH3-CHBr-CH3 (Markovnikov: H adds to C with more H)

name: Alkynes
hybridization: sp at C≡C (180° linear); sp³/sp² elsewhere
geometry: Linear around triple bond; no cis/trans at C≡C
bondType: One σ + two π (C≡C); terminal C-H is acidic (pKa ~25)
physicalProperties: IR: ≡C-H ~3300 cm⁻¹ (sharp), C≡C 2100-2260 cm⁻¹ (weak); ¹H NMR acetylenic H δ 1.8-3.1 ppm; terminal alkyne H δ ~2.5 ppm
chemicalProperties: Addition (2 equiv can add); acidic terminal H → acetylide anion; electrophilic & nucleophilic character
reactions: HC≡C⁻ Na⁺ + CH3Br → HC≡C-CH3 (alkylation via acetylide)
HC≡CH + H2O —HgSO4/H2SO4→ CH3CHO (Kucherov, enol → aldehyde via tautomerization)

name: Aromatic Hydrocarbons (Arenes)
generalFormula: CnH2n-6 (benzene family); Hückel rule: 4n+2 π e⁻ in planar cyclic conjugation
hybridization: sp² all carbons; hexagonal planar 120°; resonance delocalization 150 pm (between single 154 and double 134 pm)
geometry: Planar ring; resonance energy ~150 kJ/mol stabilization
bondType: Conjugated π system (6 p orbitals overlapping); aromatic sextet
physicalProperties: IR: aromatic C-H ~3030 cm⁻¹, C=C ~1500-1600 cm⁻¹ (2 bands), overtone 1650-2000 cm⁻¹; ¹H NMR δ 7-8 ppm (ring current); UV strong absorption; higher density/bp than aliphatic
chemicalProperties: Electrophilic aromatic substitution (EAS) retains aromaticity; NOT addition (addition would destroy aromaticity). Activating groups (-OH, -OCH3, -NH2, -alkyl) o/p-directors; deactivating (-NO2, -COOH, -CF3) m-directors; halogens deactivating but o/p-directing.

name: Cycloalkanes
hybridization: sp³; ring strain: cyclopropane 60° (high), cyclobutane 90°, cyclopentane ~108°, cyclohexane 109.5° (strain-free chair)
geometry: Chair (cyclohexane most stable): axial/equatorial positions; ring flips interconvert
bondType: σ only; angle strain + torsional strain determine reactivity
physicalProperties: Similar to acyclic; cyclohexane bp 81°C; density ~0.78; used as non-polar solvent
chemicalProperties: Like alkanes but small rings (3-4) undergo ring-opening addition due to strain
